title: Cofinality: approaching limits, regular and singular cardinals
summary: The number of positions needed to approach a limit distinguishes regular sizes from singular ones.
abstract: Assuming choice, no countable sequence of countable ordinals can reach beyond every countable ordinal. Yet some larger cardinals can be approached by countable sequences of smaller ordinals. For a limit ordinal, cofinality measures the shortest length of a sequence reaching beyond every smaller ordinal. An infinite cardinal is regular when such an approach requires as many terms as its own size, and singular when fewer suffice. This distinction also answers a concrete size question: exactly for regular cardinals, a union of fewer sets, each of smaller size, must remain smaller.
